scoring_justification: T1 recompute: peak positions and amplitudes are recomputed from raw CSV data; bond angle amplitude and Voronoi fractions are recomputed from raw JSON/CSV. These are compared against paper‑reported gold values (peak positions at 300 K, required fraction range) and required temperature trends, with tolerances that account for implementation spread.

hidden_assets.purpose: gold peak positions for Co‑B and B‑B partial PDFs at 300 K, and gold Voronoi fraction at 300 K; required trends for high‑temperature broadening and fraction decrease. All derived from the paper's Fig. 3 and Fig. 4 (right) and associated text.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: paper Fig. 3 and Fig. 4, and results text (Co‑B first shell 1.98 Å, B‑B first 1.85 Å, B‑B second 2.9 Å; fraction of Frank‑Kasper polyhedra 50 % at 300 K decreasing to 35 % at 1600 K).
hidden_assets.generation_method: taken directly from the paper; linear interpolation formula for Voronoi fraction as a function of temperature is derived from the two reported endpoints.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: these are the paper's own reported structural metrics, not fabricated. They are the exact quantities the reproduction must produce.

outputs.description: Partial pair distribution functions g(r) for Co-B and B-B pairs at 300 K and a higher temperature chosen by the solver (≥600 K). The checker will detect local maxima in specified r windows and compare extracted peak positions to hidden paper-reported values.
B-Co-B bond angle distribution at 300 K and the same higher temperature. The checker will identify the amplitude of the peak near 90° and verify that it decreases (broadens) with temperature.

Fraction of Frank-Kasper-like Voronoi polyhedra at 300 K and the higher temperature. The checker will verify that fractions are between 0 and 1, that the high-temperature fraction is lower than 300 K, and that the values match hidden paper-reported fractions within tolerances.

output_contract.notes: The solver must choose the higher temperature (e.g., 1000 K or 1600 K) and clearly label columns/keys accordingly. The checker recomputes structural features from the raw CSV/JSON files and compares them to hidden gold values derived from the paper. No experimental XRD comparison or elastic limit discussion is required.
